title: Stretch and fold, the basic gluten-building method
subtitle: How to strengthen a sourdough dough without kneading
excerpt: Stretch and fold is the method used to develop gluten in high-hydration sourdough doughs during bulk fermentation. Instead of kneading on the bench, you stretch the dough up and fold it over on itself in the bowl. Three or four sets builds a strong, extensible dough without overworking it.
sourceNotes: Stretch and fold as a gluten-development technique for high-hydration doughs is a standard method in modern home sourdough baking, developed as an alternative to traditional bench kneading for wetter doughs.

glossaryTerms.definition: The web of stretchy protein strands that forms when flour is mixed with water. A strong gluten network traps the gas produced by fermentation and gives bread its structure.
The ability of dough to stretch without tearing. Extensible dough can be shaped and scored without springing back or breaking.

content.text: in sourdough doughs without the sustained pressure of kneading. It works well for wet doughs (70% hydration and above) that would stick to the bench and tear under traditional kneading.
Wet your hand slightly so the dough does not stick.
Reach under one side of the dough, grab firmly, and pull it up and away from the bowl until you feel resistance.
Fold the stretched flap over to the opposite side. Rotate the bowl 90 degrees.
Repeat three more times until you have worked around the whole bowl. That is one set.

Most recipes call for three or four sets, spaced 30 minutes apart during the first 90 to 120 minutes of bulk fermentation. Leave the dough undisturbed after the last set so the gas can accumulate undisturbed.

Each fold aligns the gluten strands and redistributes the culture through the dough. The pauses between sets allow the proteins to relax and bond further. A dough given four sets of stretch and fold has comparable gluten development to a dough kneaded on the bench, but retains more of the gas produced during fermentation because it has been handled gently.
